title: Hong Kong suspends Gleneagles Hospital's eHealth registration after patient app data leak
date_note: The hospital reported the incident to the eHRSS Coordinator Office and the suspension took effect on 23 November; the hospital discovered unauthorized activity on 18 November (per the release).
org: Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong (港怡醫院)
geo_basis: hospital in Hong Kong as named in the government release; city given, exact address not stated in the release
summary: Hong Kong's Health Bureau said the eHealth record sharing system (eHRSS) registration of Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong was temporarily suspended on 23 November. The Department of Health says unauthorised activity affecting the security infrastructure of the hospital's patient app led to unauthorised access to some patients' personal data, which the hospital discovered on 18 November. DH asked for a detailed investigation report within four weeks; the Bureau says there is no evidence eHRSS was breached.
plain: Hong Kong's health authorities have temporarily cut a private hospital's access to the shared electronic health record system after unauthorised access to some patients' personal data through its patient app.
exec: A Hong Kong hospital lost access to the eHealth record sharing system after unauthorised access to some patients' personal data via its app; the Bureau says there is no evidence eHRSS itself was breached.
action: The Health Bureau says the hospital must confirm that no medical records were leaked and submit a detailed investigation report; eHRSS access returns only after the Office confirms no unacceptable security risk.
